purpose: Darbepoetin alfa is used to treat anemia, which means your body does not have enough red blood cells. It is commonly used in people with chronic kidney disease or in cancer patients whose anemia is caused by chemotherapy. It helps reduce the need for blood transfusions.
how_it_works: Your body naturally makes a protein called erythropoietin that tells your bone marrow to make red blood cells. Darbepoetin alfa works like that natural protein, signaling your bone marrow to produce more red blood cells. More red blood cells means more oxygen gets carried through your body, which helps you feel less tired and weak.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include high blood pressure, swelling in your legs or arms, headache, muscle or joint pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, tiredness, and reactions at the injection site such as redness or bruising.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning because it can increase the risk of heart attack, stroke, blood clots, and in some cancer patients it may cause tumors to grow faster or shorten survival. Your doctor will use the lowest dose possible and monitor you closely. Do not use it if you have uncontrolled high blood pressure. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain, difficulty breathing, or sudden numbness.
typical_dosing: Darbepoetin alfa is given as an injection under the skin or into a vein, usually once a week or once every two to three weeks depending on your condition. Your doctor will determine the right dose based on your lab results and will adjust it over time to keep your red blood cell levels in a safe range.
